h1: A fraud signal that is real, concentrated, and hard to transfer.
name: Overview

h1: Before the model, audit the simulator.
sub: The notebook profiles 1,852,394 transactions and 71 analytical columns, resolves a temporal split boundary, and documents the mechanics of the Sparkov generator
name: Data audit

h1: Fraud amounts are larger — and capped.
sub: Fraud transactions cluster at a much higher median amount, but their upper tail stops far below genuine transactions. Category rates are equally uneven: three o
name: Distributions

h1: Fraud is a card story, not a transaction story.
sub: Card-level profiles reveal extreme concentration: 976 of 999 cards see at least one fraud event, 91 are entirely fraudulent, and only 23 are untouched. Geograph
name: Interactions

h1: Drift is real. The boundary is the experiment.
sub: Weekly fraud rates oscillate around 0.60% in train and 0.42% in test. The split is a hard 48-second cut, not a random holdout; the boundary week and the final z
name: Temporal

h1: Unsupervised views separate fraud — with caveats.
sub: A 2D PCA projection reaches a logistic AUC of 0.816, but t-SNE and UMAP are lower and highly parameter-sensitive. Isolation Forest and LOF beat the autoencoder
name: Advanced viz

h1: At n = 1.85M, significance is cheap. Effect size is not.
sub: The notebook reports Mann–Whitney tests, Cliff's delta with bootstrap intervals, cluster-robust logistic regression and χ²/Cramér's V. Almost every test is sign
name: Statistics

h1: The best descriptive features are not the most transferable.
sub: Velocity, combination flags, merchant shrinkage and hour encodings are engineered and tested here. Several are strong descriptive signals. Their cross-boundary
name: Feature lab

h1: The model ranks well. The boundary is the story.
sub: A 27-feature LightGBM reaches test PR-AUC 0.5575 and ROC-AUC 0.9677, but the test split begins 48 seconds after training ends and is almost perfectly separable
name: Model

name: Economics
